text: The Marlow Medal and Prize is an early-career award in physical chemistry presented by the Royal Society of Chemistry. Each year, one or two recipients, who are junior researchers under the age of 35 or within 10 years of completing their doctorate, are selected to receive £2000 and deliver lectures at universities across the UK. The award was founded in 1957 and honors the chemist George Stanley Withers Marlow (1889–1948). Additionally, award winners are entitled to £3000 in travel expenses to participate in a lecture tour in Australia, New Zealand, Singapore, or Malaysia. This lecture series, established in 1981, is named in memory of Robert Anthony Robinson (1903–1979).
